<div class="accordion-item"><h2 class="accordion-header"><button class="accordion-button collapsed" type="button" data-bs-toggle="collapse" data-bs-target="#work-acc-summary">Summary</button></h2><div id="work-acc-summary" class="accordion-collapse collapse"><div class="accordion-body">Bhāmahavivaraṇa is a Sanskrit commentary on the Kāvyalakṣaṇa, an earlier work on poetics by Bhāmaha. It is written by Udbhaṭṭa, and it provides a detailed analysis and explanation of Bhāmaha’s Kāvyalakṣaṇa, which deals with the principles of literary aesthetics and the art of composing poetry. Udbhaṭṭa’s commentary elaborates on Bhāmaha’s ideas and adds his own insights and interpretations.<br><br>Bhāmahavivaraṇa is an important text in the field of Sanskrit poetics and has contributed to the development of Indian literary criticism. It has been studied and commented upon by later scholars, including Abhinavagupta, who wrote his own commentary on it. Bhāmahavivaraṇa, along with the Kāvyalakṣaṇa, remains an influential work on poetics in the Sanskrit tradition.</div></div></div>
<div class="accordion-item"><h2 class="accordion-header"><button class="accordion-button collapsed" type="button" data-bs-toggle="collapse" data-bs-target="#work-acc-contents">Contents</button></h2><div id="work-acc-contents" class="accordion-collapse collapse"><div class="accordion-body">Bhāmahavivaraṇa, written by Udbhaṭṭa, is a commentary on Bhāmaha’s Kāvyalakṣaṇa, which is a treatise on poetics. The work is divided into ten chapters and provides a detailed analysis and explanation of Bhāmaha’s concepts and ideas on various literary devices and figures of speech.<br><br>The first chapter of Bhāmahavivaraṇa deals with the concept of rasa, or emotional flavour, in poetry. The second chapter focuses on the different types of poetic composition and their characteristics. The third chapter discusses the various types of figures of speech, such as simile, metaphor, and hyperbole, and their functions in poetry. The fourth chapter analyses the concept of dhvani, or suggestion, in poetry. The fifth chapter discusses the importance of alaṅkāra, or ornamentation, in poetry. The sixth chapter deals with the concept of vākrokti, or indirect expression, in poetry.<br><br>The seventh chapter analyses the use of different types of meters and their significance in poetry. The eighth chapter discusses the concept of guna, or quality, in poetry. The ninth chapter analyses the importance of rīti, or style, in poetry. Finally, the tenth chapter deals with the concept of rasa-dhvani, or the emotional suggestion in poetry, and how it is related to the overall meaning and message of a poem. Overall, Bhāmahavivaraṇa is an important work of Sanskrit poetics and provides valuable insights into the art of poetry.</div></div></div>
<div class="accordion-item"><h2 class="accordion-header"><button class="accordion-button collapsed" type="button" data-bs-toggle="collapse" data-bs-target="#work-acc-uniqueness">Uniqueness</button></h2><div id="work-acc-uniqueness" class="accordion-collapse collapse"><div class="accordion-body">The uniqueness of Udbhaṭṭa's Bhāmahavivaraṇa lies in its comprehensive and in-depth analysis of Bhāmaha’s Kāvyalakṣaṇa. Through his commentary, Udbhaṭṭa not only provides a clear and concise explanation of the various literary devices mentioned by Bhāmaha, but also offers his own critical insights and interpretations. The work is also unique in the sense that it combines the theories of both Bhāmaha and Daṇḍin, making it a valuable resource for students and scholars of Sanskrit poetics.</div></div></div>
<div class="accordion-item"><h2 class="accordion-header"><button class="accordion-button collapsed" type="button" data-bs-toggle="collapse" data-bs-target="#work-acc-contribution">Contribution &amp; Notes</button></h2><div id="work-acc-contribution" class="accordion-collapse collapse"><div class="accordion-body">Bhāmahavivaraṇa by Udbhaṭṭa is a significant contribution to Sanskrit literary criticism. Through his detailed analysis and commentary on Bhāmaha’s Kāvyalakṣaṇa, Udbhaṭṭa not only clarifies and expands upon the ideas presented by Bhāmaha, but also adds his own insights and interpretations. The work thus serves as an important source for understanding the development of Sanskrit literary theory and the various schools of thought that emerged during this period. Additionally, Bhāmahavivaraṇa also provides valuable insights into the creative process of poetry and the techniques used by poets to craft their works.<br><br>Bhāmahavivaraṇa by Udbhaṭṭa is considered to be one of the most important commentaries on Bhāmaha’s Kāvyalakṣaṇa. It is also noteworthy for its detailed explanations and insights into the various figures of speech and poetic devices mentioned in Bhāmaha’s work. Additionally, the commentary is written in a clear and concise style, making it accessible to both scholars and lay readers. Bhāmahavivaraṇa is also seen as an important bridge between the early period of Sanskrit poetics and the later period, as it provides a valuable link between Bhāmaha’s work and later works such as the Kāvya Prakāśa by Mammaṭa.</div></div></div>
